title: Hemispheric failover strategy and model-tier safety buffer for dedicated→hosted transitions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define and implement a hemispheric (geo‑aware) failover policy plus a model‑tier safety buffer to safely transition requests from Dedicated capacity to Hosted tiers. The feature should limit blast radius during cross‑region evacuations, maintain SLA targets for high‑priority tenants, and ensure predictable model‑variant demotion behavior when quantized or lower‑capacity variants are used as fallback. Key goals: preserve latency SLO for P0 tenants where possible, provide bounded cost growth for hosted spillover, and implement deterministic throttles to avoid chaotic global floods.
acceptance_criteria: Hemispheric preference implemented: requests prefer same‑hemisphere regions before cross‑hemisphere failover
Safety buffer layer enforces a per‑tenant token budget for hosted spillover (configurable), preventing unbounded hosted cost during region evacuation
Model‑variant demotion window defined (grace period + degraded mode) with deterministic rollback on recovery
End‑to‑end e2e and perf tests pass for single‑tenant and multi‑tenant evacuation scenarios (latency and error budgets validated)
Runbook updated and on‑call trained for staged demote and rollback procedure
design_decisions: Use hemispheric affinity: prefer same hemisphere peers (NA <-> EU considered cross‑hemisphere only when same hemisphere capacity exhausted)
Introduce a two‑tier safety buffer: (1) soft reserve tokens for immediate hosted spillover, (2) hard cap with token throttle per minute
Model variant demotion uses staged logits: first try quantized-compatible variant of same architecture, then fallback to smaller arch only if latency SLO allows
Avoid global broadcast fallbacks: routing changes stamped and phased with randomized jitter to prevent thundering herd
Expose tenant‑level spill quota to billing/console for transparency and chargeback
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Simulation run in staging with synthetic tenant mixes and hemispheric capacity loss (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Canary in production on 5 low‑risk tenants with telemetry gating (1 week)
Phase 2: Gradual cohort expansion + monitor cost/latency, enable token buffer enforcement for additional tenants (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Global enablement with default conservative buffers and documented upgrade path for tenants to opt into higher spill budgets
monitoring_and_alerting: SLOs: p50/p95/p99 latency for P0 and P1 tenants during transitions
Alert: token_buffer_utilization > 85% for 5 minutes (priority P0 paging)
Alert: model_variant_demote_rate spike > threshold (investigate degradation cause)
tests: Load test: 10k rps synthetic tenant mix while killing entire NA primary region to validate hemispheric fallback
Chaos test: staggered region outages with randomized recovery timings to exercise phased rollbacks
Cost test: verify per‑tenant hosted cost stays within configured hard cap under sustained overload
Regression: ensure no increase in cold‑start latency for warm standby lanes during transitions
